name: Valhalla
description: Valhalla is an open-source routing engine and accompanying libraries for use with OpenStreetMap data. It provides turn-by-turn routing, map matching (snapping noisy GPS traces to the road/path network), time+distance matrices, isochrones and elevation lookups over a self-built tile graph. Commonly run as a self-hosted routing backend so that location data never has to be sent to a third party.

notes.text: Compiled from source on first install - there is no official Debian/Ubuntu package. Expect the install to take 20-45+ minutes depending on CPU/RAM.

No routing tiles are built during install, since that requires an OSM extract for the region you actually travel in. Run /opt/valhalla_data/build-tiles.sh <geofabrik-pbf-url> afterwards, e.g. with a https://download.geofabrik.de extract for your country. Avoid planet-wide data unless the container is sized for it.
The HTTP API (used for /status, /trace_route, /trace_attributes, etc.) listens on port 8002 with no authentication - keep it on a private/internal network.

To use this as the map-matching backend for GeoPulse, set GEOPULSE_TIMELINE_MAP_MATCHING_ENABLED=true, GEOPULSE_TIMELINE_MAP_MATCHING_PROVIDER=valhalla and GEOPULSE_TIMELINE_MAP_MATCHING_VALHALLA_BASE_URL=http://<this-container-IP>:8002 on the GeoPulse backend.
Updating rebuilds Valhalla from source at the latest GitHub release tag; existing tiles/config in /opt/valhalla_data are left untouched.

The default 24GB disk / 8192MB RAM only covers the build. A country-sized Geofabrik extract needs roughly 4-8x its compressed size in free disk for tiles, and building/updating wants more RAM than steady-state serving - resize the container before running build-tiles.sh or before updating if you shrank it after the initial install.
